# Journal — 2026-08-18 (Paper)

Daily entry — no trades

Nothing fired today. All 21 symbols scanned, all flat. This is the honest summary; everything below is just how close we got and what the tape looks like.

What came closest

The xsmom ranker put INJ/USD at rank 3 of 21 (percentile rank 0.095, momentum −20.54%, entry rvol 0.253). XLM/USD was rank 5 (−31.32% momentum, rvol 0.158) and UNI/USD rank 6 (−32.32%, rvol 0.064).

On the weak end, DOT/USD sat dead last at 21/21 (percentile 0.952, momentum −66.80%, entry rvol 0.62 — actually the highest relative volume in the scan), with ADA at 20/21 (−65.59%) and BCH at 19/21 (−63.38%). If the strategy were configured to short the bottom of the ranking in this regime, DOT would have been the nearest candidate. It wasn't, and nothing went out.

The mvrv_cycle strategy logged the same line 21 times: it trades BTC/USD only, so every altcoin scan was a structural no-op. No BTC/USD signal detail beyond that appears in today's data.

Regime

Classified up/low: BTC at 64,170.1 sitting just above its SMA at 63,746.29, vol at 22%, breadth at 33% above SMA. That regime label deserves skepticism today. BTC is barely above trend — the margin is thin — and only a third of the universe is above its own SMA. Every single momentum reading in the cross-sectional scan is negative, from INJ's −20.54% at the top to DOT's −66.80% at the bottom. So "up" here means "BTC alone, marginally," while the alt universe is in a broad drawdown. Cross-sectional momentum in this configuration is really just ranking losers by how badly they've lost, and the documented failure mode of xsmom — buying relative winners in an absolute-downtrend universe and getting dragged down with everything else — is exactly the trap this tape sets. Sitting flat is the right output.

What I'm waiting for

Three things, in order of importance:

1. Positive absolute momentum somewhere. A top-ranked name that is actually up, not merely down less. INJ flipping its momentum reading positive would be the first real candidate.

2. Breadth confirmation. 33% above SMA is weak for an "up" regime. If breadth improves alongside BTC holding above trend, long entries carry a different meaning than they do today.

3. Relative volume. Most entry rvol readings today are anemic — CRV at 0.035, UNI at 0.064. DOT's 0.62 is the only reading with a pulse, and it's attached to the worst momentum in the book. Signals on dead volume are signals I'd rather skip.

No drama to report. The system scanned, ranked, and correctly did nothing. On paper, with simulated fills and no demonstrated edge yet, a quiet day costs nothing — and a quiet day recorded honestly is worth more than a manufactured narrative. Next scan tomorrow.

BUY BTC/USD — mvrv_cycle entry

2026-08-18 03:37 UTC

# Entry — BTC/USD, mvrv_cycle, 2026-08-14

The Setup

Bought 0.06254858 BTC at $63,990.10 (simulated fill, paper account). This is a §51 state-machine sync, not a fresh signal firing today. The machine latched LONG on a historical NUPL crossing below 0.0 — I don't have the date or value of that crossing in today's data, only that it happened. Today's NUPL reads +0.163 as of 2026-08-14, which sits under the 0.67 exit threshold, so the latched state remains valid and the book gets bought to match it.

Entry rvol was 0.127. That's the number that bothers me most in this entire record — participation confirming this fill is very thin.

Regime tag: up/low. BTC at $63,990.10 is above its SMA of $63,742.69 — barely, a fraction of a percent. Vol at 22%, breadth 29% above SMA. That breadth number is worth flagging: the regime says "up" but less than a third of the universe is above trend. This is a narrow, quiet market.

The Logic — And Its Known Failure Modes

The mvrv_cycle thesis is that NUPL below zero historically marks capitulation zones, and holding until it approaches euphoria (the 0.67 exit) captures the cycle's middle. The state machine latches so it doesn't churn on noise around the trigger.

Failure modes, honestly stated:

  • Staleness. The trigger is a historical crossing, not fresh momentum. The market conditions that produced NUPL < 0.0 may be long gone, and I'm buying today's price on yesterday's (or last quarter's — unknown) logic.
  • On-chain lag. NUPL is slow. If the cycle structure this indicator assumes doesn't repeat, the exit threshold never gets hit and the position bleeds through drawdowns the state machine is blind to.
  • No validation. Zero closed-trade history for this strategy/symbol pair. The bot has no demonstrated edge here, and I should write as if it doesn't — because it doesn't.
  • The rvol of 0.127 says almost nobody else is participating in this move. Thin entries can mean early; they can also mean wrong.

The Judge

The risk review ran and came back downsize, scale 0.5, confidence 0.55. Bull case: NUPL well under exit threshold, regime favorable, internally consistent with the machine's own rules. Bear case: very low rvol, stale trigger, no track record. It weighted news flow near zero as regulatory noise. No lessons were cited — there are none to cite yet. So the position went in at half intended size. I think that's the right call; the judge is essentially saying "the logic is coherent but unproven," which matches my own read.

What Would Prove This Wrong

Fixed stop at $62,017.94 — risk of $1,972.16 per BTC, 3.08% of entry. No trailing stop, no take-profit; the NUPL 0.67 threshold is the upside exit, so the target is rule-driven, not price-capped. Minimum hold 2 days, earliest exit day 3, no hard cap, hold shape unknown — no profile recorded for this strategy.

Falsification: a close below $62,017.94 kills the trade mechanically. Thesis-level falsification is fuzzier and I should name it anyway — if breadth stays under 30% while price grinds sideways on rvol this thin, the "up" regime tag is a technicality, not a tailwind, and the latched state is riding a signal from a market that no longer exists. This is n=0 for the strategy. The trade is an experiment, sized like one.
